sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Party Cruisers is a growing events and wedding-services business with real operating scale, but the investment case should remain on a reliability watchlist. Revenue reached ₹146.83 crore and owners PAT ₹12.56 crore in FY26; CFO was only ₹4.19 crore. The right distinction is fixed-asset-light versus working-capital-light: the latter is not established. Venue advances and customer collection timing absorb substantial capital.

Business Quality is 5.1/10 and Growth Quality 5.0/10 after the persistent-cash-conversion ceiling. Investment Attractiveness is NS. These are descriptive assessments, not ranked recommendations: G2 is Hold. A conditional funded base yields 18.01% annually at the verified ₹98.95 close, but that is not an ordinary supported return or a buy price. The bear path fails the cash reserve before the rights application receipt and later; without explicit rescue its return is deliberately blank. An explicit discounted rescue still loses money over five years. Thin SME liquidity materially limits implementation even at the illustrative ₹5 lakh position.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Research cutoff:20 October 2026. Market reference:official 19 October 2026 NSE close ₹98.95, not a live quotation. Issuer:Party Cruisers Limited, ISIN INE06ZX01015, tickerPARTYCRUS, NSE SME, seriesSM, lot 1,000. The legal identity is cross-checked against the exact ISIN rather than copying typographical CIN variants in several company headers. Currency is nominal INR; financial tables use crore unless otherwise labeled. Accounting-basis wording is inconsistent: the FY26 parent audit introduction refers to Ind AS, while the financial notes use Indian GAAP and AS17/AS20, with cancellable operating rent expensed rather than an Ind AS116 lease balance. We follow the disclosed AS-style statements and expense rentals; we do not assert a verified Ind AS transition or capitalize a fabricated right-of-use asset. The investment horizon runs exactly 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031; the hurdle is 15% pretax, with 12% and 18% alternatives. No personal portfolio suitability is inferred.

The primary annual reports, signed financial statements, rights offer, allotment and dated exchange files are the evidence base. Facts, management assertions, analyst assumptions and inferences are separately labeled. G1 is Conditional, G2 Hold, G3 Conditional and G4 Conditional. Main opinions are distinguished from CARO, IFC, audit-trail reporting and earlier qualifications. FY26 parent CARO and both actual IFC annexures were inspected; unmodified opinions are not treated as blanket assurance of every disclosure. Old audit exceptions, FD availability, future calls and current pledge/surveillance details remain explicit limitations.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
All 13 factors use the same primitive integer or NS wherever repeated. GOV4, MOAT4, REV8, DUR6, CAP6, CASH3, BAL6, EXEC5, EARN7, R NS, D4, P NS and L1. The exact BQS weighted sum is 5.06; the raw GQS is 6.65, reduced to 5 because persistent weak cash realization is supported across the latest three years. R and P are not filled with neutral scores. IAS coverage is 0.55; its known weighted contribution is 2.1650 and diagnostic bounds are['2.6150', '6.6650']. Those bounds are not a ranked IAS.

BQS weights are 20/20/12/10/12/10/8/8 for GOV/MOAT/REV/DUR/CAP/CASH/BAL/EXEC. GQS weights are 40/20/15/15/10 for REV/DUR/EARN/CAP/CASH. IAS weights are 25% unrounded final BQS,35% R,20% D,10% P and 10% L. Decimal arithmetic and HALF_UP one-decimal displays are retained separately from the raw values. GOV is above 3, G1 is not Fail and G3 is not an observed Fail, so the severe-failure 3-point caps do not apply. The GQS5-point cash ceiling does. All ranking flags remain false because financial reliability is on Hold.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The business plans and delivers weddings, social events and corporate events; it also supplies event décor, flowers and related services. It combines design and logistics with vendor/venue coordination, with domestic operations and a small Dubai/subsidiary contribution. Revenue is not a pure software-like fee stream. Hotels, event production and materials are large purchased inputs, and changes between material cost and event/hotel expense categories mean that revenue less materials would fabricate an economic gross margin. Gross profit/value added is therefore ND.

The forward-booking extension is important: management reserves hotel, banquet or convention capacity ahead of customer collection, potentially earning a spread but also carrying cancellation, timing and counterparty exposure. A client token does not necessarily fund the venue obligation. The annual statements show customer advances, but not sustainable negative working capital. Operating premises are rented on cancellable leases; rent remains a recurring operating cost in the model. Neither leased assets nor operating deposits are given a second sum-of-parts value. Brand names establish the product offering, not a network effect or a barrier to entry.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The defensible positive case is execution know-how, established vendor relationships, brand recognition and the ability to coordinate complex events. Standalone expansion is too large to dismiss as merely acquired revenue. Nevertheless, wedding customers are often episodic, competitive offerings are numerous and procurement can be replicated. No primary retained-client cohort, net revenue retention, pricing-premium history, exclusive venue tenure or market-share series was found. We therefore assign MOAT4, not a premium for celebrity names or a fashionable event-spending story.

Venue exclusivity could create an advantage only if contracts are enforceable, renewal economics attractive and blocked dates can be resold without material loss. Management’s statement that transferable advances carry no capital-loss risk is not accepted as an economic guarantee. The Wizcraft deposit illustrates why deposits are not interchangeable with bank cash, without implying that every venue advance is similarly distressed. There is no reliable directly comparable listed pure-play dataset in this research; terminal multiples are clearly analyst ranges rather than a claimed peer discount. Strong historic incremental returns are evaluated under CAP, not duplicated as automatic moat evidence.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
The six-point history is FY21₹8.8842 crore, FY22₹15.5507 crore, FY23₹39.7837 crore, FY24₹63.5451 crore, FY25₹116.49562 crore and FY26₹146.828767 crore. The five-year CAGR is 75.24%, heavily distorted by the pandemic starting year. The more relevant standalone FY23–FY26 CAGR is 52.00%; the group CAGR over the same interval is 54.54%. FY26 group growth is 26.04%, below the previous surge but still substantial. The group/standalone scope difference is disclosed rather than treated as a precise organic-sales bridge.

The revenue rubric gives 9 mechanically for growth above 30%, but only three relevant post-trough years and medium-confidence classification justify an 8 ceiling. There is no extra point for margins. FY25 source revenue categories misleadingly place most sales under scrap; the FY26 comparative reassigns most to event décor while the total stays consistent. The changed labels must not be interpreted as a genuine shift from scrap trading to weddings without explanation. Event counts, average spend, cancellations, retained net fees and customer concentration remain unavailable. Nominal top-line growth is established more strongly than underlying volume growth.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
A bottom-up event-count model is not supportable because event counts, venue capacity and retained fee per booking are not disclosed. The substitute is an explicit service-business revenue/operating-margin path with matching advance days, receivable days, capex and dated financing. Base FY27–FY32 revenue growth is 18/16/14/12/10/8%, below the recent three-year rate. The base EBIT margin is 11.3%, after operating rent and recurring costs; gross margin is not known. The base venue-advance assumption is 60 days of annual revenue; receivables 55 days, customer advances 10 days and payables 6 days. Seasonality is an analyst assumption, not a verified booking ledger.

The FY23–FY26 NOPAT change at a 25% normalized tax rate is ₹7.632 crore against an invested-capital increase of ₹14.941 crore, a 51.1% proxy. The denominator includes full equity/debt/NCI less separately identified cash/investments, not just PPE. This acknowledges efficient historical expansion, but qualified opening balances, category inconsistencies and much greater prospective advances prevent extrapolating that return. An operating-asset cross-check gives broad capital of ₹21.5867 crore in FY23 and ₹40.9984 crore in FY26: PPE decreases ₹1.3971 crore while broad net working assets increase ₹20.8088 crore. The resulting ₹19.4117 crore increase differs from the financing-side ₹14.9414 crore by ₹4.4703 crore, exactly explained within rounding by provisions net of deferred-tax assets rising from ₹0.2411 crore to ₹4.7114 crore. This numerical operating-asset bridge reconciles to financing IC; it is not an unexplained plug. Cumulative FY24–FY26 cash capex ₹5.1159 crore less D&A₹6.0254 crore implies ₹0.9094 crore PPE decline versus actual ₹1.3971 crore;₹0.4876 crore disposal/scope/reclassification residual is left unallocated. The bridge strengthens the conclusion that working assets, not fixed assets, dominate reinvestment; it does not eliminate accounting qualification risk. A nominal 12–16% capital-cost band is an analyst hurdle, not a sourced WACC. CAP6 is a mixed-evidence judgment, not a dismissal for lacking private project cohorts. Persistent poor cash conversion separately caps GQS at 5.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Founder-family involvement is central. The two principal managing directors together held 7.695 million shares at March 2026; that is not a complete promoter-group shareholding or a current free-float estimate. The September rights offer says promoters would not subscribe. Post-issue promoter percentages and pledges require a fresh primary shareholding filing; secondary snapshots are not substituted. FY26 disclosed director remuneration is ₹0.80282 crore, with additional family rent, car-rental and consultation transactions. The proposed monthly pay ceilings could materially change recurring costs if used; caps are not treated as actual expenses.

Capital history includes the 2021IPO, the 2023one-for-one bonus, preferential warrant conversion and ESOP exercises, and the 2026partly paid rights issue. The model distinguishes paid capital from future calls and tests a conservative option count because the disclosed movement table does not add up. An earlier 2022preferential proposal was withdrawn after the proposed investor lacked funds, a historical example rather than a current default. Execution evidence is strong sales growth, not automatic achievement of the 50-partner target. Pending legal allegations are summarized without inferring guilt. Transparency about old qualifications, Tally logging, options, cash reclassifications and actual remuneration is the most useful near-term governance test.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY26 cash conversion is 33.1% and the FY24–FY26 cumulative ratio is 53.8%. The closing-receivable/revenue proxy increases from 32.07 days in FY25 to 55.08 in FY26; average-balance DSO is separately calculated and is not interchangeable with that proxy. Advances to vendors jump to ₹9.2483537 crore; government balances of ₹7.7159259 crore are not available cash. Other current liabilities include ₹4.681211 crore statutory dues and ₹4.1517272 crore customer advances. Treating the entire liability increase as repeatable client funding would overstate quality. Tax provision ₹4.8356377 crore and gratuity ₹0.8020226 crore are preserved in the funding bridge.

Audit history is not clean throughout:FY22 results have a disclaimer, FY23 is qualified with an indicated ₹0.41 crore adjustment, and FY24/FY25 retain old-receivable qualifications. Current FY26 main opinions and actual IFC opinions are unmodified, an important improvement; CARO reports no loan default or reported fraud. However, the old-balance resolution was not specifically traced and database audit logging remains an exception in the contemporaneous rights-offer audit. FY26 annual exception tables are absent on the rendered pages.

Not every difference is an error:FY25FD and tax classification changes are bridged without double counting. By contrast, the FY24 cash-flow comparative inAR2025 fails its arithmetic and repeats a prior extraordinary charge, the ESOP table omits 93,441grants from its movement arithmetic, and consolidated EPS uses group rather than owners PAT. These unresolved matters justify G2 Hold, not a fraud label. All original/revised amounts and limitations remain embedded with the financial history.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹98.95, the 11,989,913 fully paid shares imply ₹118.6402 crore quoted fully paid capitalization. Multiplying every partly paid share by the fully paid price without accounting for ₹90unpaid calls is not a clean market-cap measure. The conditional terminal denominator includes all 1,876,676rights shares and 1,039,825future options, for 14,906,414 shares. Calls and option exercise proceeds enter the cash bridge only on explicitly assumed dates. An investor buying the existing fully paid share is not assumed to buy new rights or personally pay calls on someone else’s partly paid shares.

The base uses 8 times terminal operating EBIT, the bear 6 times and bull 10 times. These are analyst ranges for contestable services, not a verified peer multiple. OperatingEV plus terminal cash minus the retained ₹2 crore reserve, debt, residual gratuity and a distinct NCI claim gives common equity. No extra value is assigned to operating deposits/property, and no post-terminal call proceeds leak into value. The terminal earnings are the forward FY32 annual run-rate at October 2031, not historical TTM or a completed FY32. A separate no-future-call/no-option-cash stress retains all partly paid rights claims and conservative unexercised-option dilution without inventing forfeiture. It remains conditionally funded, with minimum cash ₹4.282 crore and a 16.73% five-year conditional return. By contrast, excluding half the opening FDs or moving more advances before entry breaches the reserve. These results show that advance timing and cash availability, not simply whether every future call is collected, drive the funding judgment. The exact five-year base conditional IRR is 18.01% and bull 33.93%; ordinary IRRs/entry prices are NS under G2 Hold. Funded constant-growth solvers at 12/15/18% hurdles are fully bracketed and include cash constraints. Genuine advance-days×multiple and capex×reserve matrices show how valuation and financeability interact rather than just printing isolated price targets.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The plausible adverse sequence is early venue cash outflow, delayed customer receipts, delayed rights calls, weaker margins and a cancellation loss. The no-rescue bear assumes no FY27 growth, slower subsequent expansion,8% EBIT margin,75 days each of receivables/vendor advances,₹2 crore venue loss,₹2.2231313 crore tax contingencies and calls deferred into FY28. Minimum pre-entry cash is ₹-4.761 crore and the full-path minimum ₹-12.392 crore against a ₹2 crore reserve. These are modeled gaps, not an allegation that the actual company defaulted.

No terminal price, no-rescue IRR or hurdle entry price is reported on that failed path, even though a terminal accounting equity number can be computed. A separate rescue subscribes whole shares at ₹79.16, a 20% discount to the reference price, with 3% fees, before each interval’s uses. It requires 1,874,310 new shares and gives the rescue investors 11.17% of the final shares; rescue share expansion relative to the no-rescue terminal count is 12.57%. Aggregate rescue gross, fees and net are ₹14.8370,₹0.4451 and ₹14.3919 crore respectively. Ownership dilution is not the same as share expansion. Even after rescue the existing-share conditional IRR is-5.95%. Independent stresses for unavailableFDs, parent-only cash, faster advance build and delayed calls isolate the cause of any gap. Lowering an analyst cash floor can change funding status but does not prove financial safety.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A multibagger claim is not the central thesis. Over five years,5 times and 10 times share value require approximately 38.0 % and 58.5% annual per-share returns. The reported pandemic recovery growth rate does not make those returns a normal expectation. Future revenue must convert into owners earnings, additional advances must be funded, and dilution from rights/options must be included before discussing per-share outcomes. Multiple expansion cannot be assumed to repair poor cash realization.

The explicit bull template is ambitious:FY27–FY32 growth 25/22/20/18/15/12%,13% operating margin and 10 times operatingEBIT. Its conditional annual return is below the five-year 5 times threshold. That is a useful feasibility boundary, not proof that 5 times is impossible. A stronger outcome would require more growth, better margins, less capital absorption or a higher valuation than this already favorable set. With G2 Hold and weak liquidity, presenting 5 times or 10 times as a target would offer precision unsupported by the financial evidence. The appropriate work is to verify collections and venue economics before increasing the growth hypothesis.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
First priority is evidence that changes reliability, not another revenue headline:obtain the aged-qualified-receivable collection/write-off bridge; reconcile FY24 cash-flow/asset comparatives; confirm current Tally database logging; reconcile the ESOP movement and fully diluted common-owner EPS. Resolve those items before reopening a ranked investment conclusion. Request current FD availability and a complete parent/group bank-and-debt bridge without assuming that the absence of private daily statements alone proves distress.

For each rights call, verify board notice, due date, actual receipts, arrears/forfeitures and utilization. Track advance balances by venue, cancellation/transfer terms, event dates and customer receipts. Compare quarterly/half-year receivable days with 55 days, cash conversion with the three-year 54% benchmark, and statutory dues with their actual settlement rather than accepting permanent rollover. Check the disclosed 1 December 2026Wizcraft hearing through official subsequent filings; it is not a promise to monitor automatically. Reconcile actual remuneration against the new caps. Before implementation, refresh primary promoter/pledge data, surveillance restrictions, bid–ask depth and whole-lot capacity for the investor’s real position. Favorable triggers require more than growth; adverse triggers include aged balances, unavailable cash or fresh issue dependence.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Classification:high reported growth with material reliability, cash-conversion and implementation reservations. The business-quality score is mixed, not a compounder certification. Growth Quality is constrained by weak cash realization despite fast revenues. Investment Attractiveness is NS and ordinary return/entry-price outputs remain blank. All ranking eligibility flags are false while G2 is Hold; low valuation arithmetic cannot override that gate.

The sensible next analytical step is a targeted reconciliation of financial/audit/option issues and current capital funding, followed by a fresh model and current liquidity test. A change to G2 requires evidence, not simply the passage of time or a higher stock price. The base funding template acknowledges positive published cash and low debt; it does not force a funding Hold solely because daily statements are private. Conversely, the failing bear cannot be promoted to a normal return by plugging the shortfall or ignoring a pre-entry breach. This report is research at the stated cutoff, not a personalized order, position-size recommendation, promise of liquidity or assurance of future return.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary sources comprise six annual-year account histories, current annual-report and rights-offer audits, the September corrigendum, the 14 Octoberallotment, the dated security master and 60validated bhavcopies. Every source has its exact URL, retrieval date and file hash where available. Financial extracts are factual and source-safe; reproduction verifies arithmetic from those extracts rather than re-authenticating an absent original PDF. Amounts rounded to thousands in older statements remain at that precision. Facts, management projections, inferences and assumptions are not blended.

Forward growth, seasonality, operating margins, capex, advance days, legacy-liability settlement dates, FD availability, the ₹2 crore reserve, rights-call dates, option exercises, NCI valuation and terminal multiples are analyst assumptions. Ordinary current returns are unsupported; funded scenario outputs are conditional. Outstanding questions include the old audit qualifications and current logging, exact option count, venue-level cancellation economics, receivable collections, FD restrictions, current primary promoter pledges, surveillance status and management target delivery. Absence of proof is labeled as a gap, not misconduct. The complete canonical contains all annual financial rows, every dated scenario row, sensitivity cells, solver scans, factor calculations, evidence and source registers, so conclusions can be checked without a detached spreadsheet.

evidence.claim: Party Cruisers Limited is NSE PARTYCRUS, ISIN INE06ZX01015, SME series SM. The official 19 October 2026 close is ₹98.95 and the trading lot is 1,000 shares.
evidence.qualification: Inactive series are not alternatives to the active SM quote. Some company headers retain the old U-prefix CIN; issuer identity is verified by the exact ISIN.

evidence.claim: Revenue increases from ₹8.8842 crore in FY21 to ₹146.828767 crore in FY26. The FY23–FY26 standalone comparison is ₹39.7837 crore to ₹139.6989573 crore; subsidiaries explain only a small part of the overall expansion.
evidence.locator: Annual financial statements and consolidated-subsidiary other-matters paragraph
evidence.qualification: The pandemic trough is not a sustainable growth base. The company does not disclose event-count, pricing and organic-volume attribution.

evidence.claim: FY26 consolidated owners PAT is ₹12.564443 crore versus group PAT of ₹12.65208 crore. Other income is ₹0.9518658 crore, operating EBIT ₹16.5902183 crore and lease rental expense ₹1.6531179 crore.
evidence.qualification: Operating rent remains an expense. Reported diluted EPS is not accepted as a fully diluted common-owner valuation denominator.

evidence.claim: FY26 CFO is ₹4.1880657 crore and cash capex ₹0.9786181 crore. Receivables absorb ₹11.9189689 crore and loans/advances ₹6.8386222 crore, while other current liabilities supply ₹7.6048927 crore.
evidence.qualification: CFO already includes working capital. Customer advances and statutory payables have different persistence; neither is counted twice.

evidence.claim: FY26 group receivables are ₹22.1559265 crore and inventory ₹2.5334489 crore. Standalone ageing includes ₹1.4239263 crore overdue one to two years and ₹12.153095 crore overdue under one year.
evidence.qualification: No individual customer confirmations or subsequent collection ledger was obtained. Overdue balances alone do not prove misconduct.

evidence.claim: Management describes venue payments three to five months before client collections, with small client tokens. It projects standalone net working capital of ₹53.397 crore in FY27 against ₹29.4262 crore in FY26, including ₹36.7851 crore of short-term advances.
evidence.qualification: These are management projections. Claims that transferable bookings eliminate capital loss are not a guarantee. Their working-capital definition differs from the model.

evidence.claim: The rights offer discloses a ₹2 crore Fairmount venue advance already paid and ₹3–4 crore Jio convention-space discussions, not a final contract. A ₹1.1 crore Wizcraft EMD/performance-deposit refund remains in insolvency-related litigation.
evidence.qualification: The Fairmount payment date relative to March is unclear. The model conservatively treats ₹2 crore as subsequent seasonal prefunding and gives no separate terminal deposit recovery.

evidence.claim: FY22 results carry a disclaimer concerning receivables of ₹1.0506 crore, payables of ₹1.7588 crore and inventory. FY23 qualifications cover ₹0.48 crore of unconfirmed receivables, payables, ₹0.1596 crore of aged receivables and ₹0.2552 crore of advances. The impact statement indicates a ₹0.41 crore adjustment and says qualifications began in FY21.
evidence.qualification: Management says some customers do not keep books and some balances subsequently settled. That is relevant counterevidence, but not a complete reconciliation.

evidence.claim: FY24 retains a ₹0.1416 crore aged-receivable qualification; FY25 retains ₹0.1422 crore. FY26 parent and consolidated main opinions are unmodified, and the actual IFC annexures express unmodified opinions.
evidence.qualification: The improved current opinion is favorable. No specific collection or write-off bridge for the old qualified balance was located; a historical qualification is not a finding of fraud.

evidence.claim: FY24/FY25 reports and the FY26 audited-results report in the rights offer disclose that Tally Prime database audit-trail logging was disabled. FY26 annual reports refer to exceptions below but omit the exception table on the rendered pages.
evidence.qualification: The omitted table is not treated as remediation. Current logging and the relationship between the audit versions require clarification.

evidence.claim: Original FY24 CFO is ₹5.5572 crore; the FY25 comparative prints ₹3.8033 crore, including a ₹1.7234 crore extraordinary deduction, and its subtotals do not reconcile to cash movement by approximately ₹1.7235 crore. FY24 assets and debt also change by ₹0.2059 crore in the next comparative without a located bridge.
evidence.qualification: The original FY24 statement is used transparently. The changed comparator is not assumed to be a valid restatement.

evidence.claim: The FY26 comparative moves ₹9 crore of FY25 FDs from current investments into cash/bank and ₹3.016633 crore of tax provision out of other current liabilities. The FY25 CFO revision of ₹0.0226773 crore approximates tax-refund-interest reclassification.
evidence.qualification: Classification changes are not automatically errors. Cash, FDs and old tax claims are each counted once.

evidence.claim: The 14 October allotment is 1,876,676 partly paid rights shares at ₹120, with ₹30 paid. Gross application receipts are ₹5.630028 crore; ₹16.890084 crore remains callable. Fully paid shares number 11,989,913; the combined count is 13,866,589 before options.
evidence.qualification: Final allotment supersedes earlier maximum issue sizes. Calls are at the board’s discretion, not received cash. The model assumes ₹0.10 crore issue fees from the offer estimate.

evidence.claim: ESOP disclosures show 81,270 plus 869,914 closing options, or 951,184 total. The second scheme arithmetic, 889,596 opening plus 93,441 grants minus 19,682 exercises, instead yields 963,355 and a combined 1,044,625. The discrepancy is 93,441 options.
evidence.qualification: The conservative scenario includes 1,039,825 future options after subtracting the 4,800 already included in the current share count. The extra arithmetic quantity is not asserted to be legally issued.

evidence.claim: FY26 group cash/bank of ₹20.7235276 crore includes ₹12.0844097 crore in FDs; parent cash is ₹19.1289275 crore. Separate assets include ₹7.7159259 crore of government balances and ₹5.1247667 crore of long-term deposits. Debt is ₹0.07668 crore.
evidence.qualification: No specific FD restriction was identified, but current maturity and availability remain unconfirmed. Parent-only cash and half-FD-unavailable sensitivities are shown.

evidence.claim: FY26 income-tax provision of ₹4.8356377 crore, statutory dues of ₹4.681211 crore and gratuity of ₹0.8020226 crore remain claims. Customer advances of ₹4.1517272 crore provide some operating funding.
evidence.qualification: Legacy income-tax and statutory claims are settled once. Future current tax is separately paid in cash; government balances are not netted without evidence.

evidence.claim: FY26 directors remuneration is ₹0.80282 crore. Disclosed related-party rent is ₹0.444 crore, car rent ₹0.36 crore and consultation ₹0.18 crore. The AGM notice seeks monthly remuneration caps of ₹10 lakh for each of two managing directors and ₹5 lakh for Armaan.
evidence.qualification: Remuneration caps are not actual expenses or automatic future commitments. Related-party dealings alone do not establish abuse.

evidence.claim: The service-tax dispute is ₹2.0589309 crore. Remaining GST/ITC exposure after disclosed payments is ₹0.1642004 crore. The rights offer also discloses pending promoter criminal proceedings and quashing petitions.
evidence.qualification: The allegations are not proven. Legal status is as disclosed in September; no speculative penalty is invented. The bear scenario pays both quantified tax contingencies.

evidence.claim: The May 2023 investor presentation targeted 50 franchise/channel partners by FY25. Revenue subsequently grew, but an authenticated 50-unit completion and mature-unit-return reconciliation were not located.
evidence.qualification: Unverified achievement is not proof of failure. Brand names and celebrity client references do not establish switching costs.

evidence.claim: All 60 official archive dates validate; 53 contain issuer rows and seven do not. The latest session trades 2,000 shares in two transactions. The observed median turnover is ₹295,450. Without imputing missing rows as zero, the complete-window median is bounded between ₹226,475 and ₹373,725.
evidence.qualification: The most favorable median bound still implies more than 26 sessions at 5% participation. Live spreads, depth, surveillance and a current primary pledge filing remain unavailable.

evidence.claim: The dated cash model explicitly includes venue advances, taxes, other claims, capex, rights applications/calls and options. Base and bull templates meet the cash floor. The no-rescue bear breaches it before entry and later; its returns remain unscored.
evidence.qualification: All forward operating inputs and future call dates are assumptions. G2 Hold suppresses ordinary return/entry outputs; an explicit rescue is a separate hypothetical transaction.

evidence.claim: The company is light in fixed assets, not necessarily in working capital. Retained profits and new equity support receivables, venue advances and tax balances. A strong historical incremental-capital proxy is subject to audit qualifications and a changing forward-booking business mix.
evidence.qualification: The proxy is not a claim about individual event cohorts. Operating commitments and cash conversion constrain the strength of the capital-efficiency conclusion.

evidence.claim: FY26 accounting-basis terminology is inconsistent: the parent audit introduction says Ind AS, while the accounts disclose Indian GAAP/AS17/AS20 and expense cancellable operating rent.
evidence.locator: Parent main opinion PDFp63; financial notes pp109–114 and operating lease disclosure.
evidence.qualification: No independently verified Ind AS transition is inferred. The model follows disclosed AS-style expense treatment, keeps rent in operating margin, and does not fabricate lease assets or liabilities.

summary:
Party Cruisers is a growing events and wedding-services business with real operating scale, but the investment case should remain on a reliability watchlist. Revenue reached ₹146.83 crore and owners PAT ₹12.56 crore in FY26; CFO was only ₹4.19 crore. The right distinction is fixed-asset-light versus working-capital-light: the latter is not established. Venue advances and customer collection timing absorb substantial capital.

Business Quality is 5.1/10 and Growth Quality 5.0/10 after the persistent-cash-conversion ceiling. Investment Attractiveness is NS. These are descriptive assessments, not ranked recommendations: G2 is Hold. A conditional funded base yields 18.01% annually at the verified ₹98.95 close, but that is not an ordinary supported return or a buy price. The bear path fails the cash reserve before the rights application receipt and later; without explicit rescue its return is deliberately blank. An explicit discounted rescue still loses money over five years. Thin SME liquidity materially limits implementation even at the illustrative ₹5 lakh position.
